summary: Restored L-6 cab rebuilt from salvaged parts in Ray Kresek's Spokane yard; NHLR-registered 1999, open by appointment. Sources disagree on L-6 count and origin.

facts.design: L-6 cab (8 x 8 ft wood USFS-design cab) rebuilt from salvaged parts, on a 6-ft wood tower; a separate 60-ft 1929 spar-tree replica stands beside it (museum page)

access.note: Open to the public by appointment, March through November; admission free; call ahead for reservations (museum page). Register says open by appointment with Ray Kresek.

events.note: The cab was honored with the highest awards at the 1984 Interstate Fair in Spokane (museum page)

corrections.proposed: standing (restored cab built from salvaged L-6 parts)
corrections.why: The register describes a restored structure assembled from salvaged parts. The museum page describes a separate 60-ft spar-tree replica beside the cab, so the replica label may belong to that structure instead.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The museum page says it is one of only two remaining L-6 towers, restored from the ruins of the last of 200. The register says the cab is parts from seven torn-down L-6s and that only three remain at original locations. The story reports both; the count is not settled.

The register gives a 6-ft wood tower under the cab. The museum page describes a separate 60-ft spar-tree replica beside it. The story treats these as separate structures, and no height is recorded for the cab.

notes_for_editor: No source dates when the cab was assembled or placed in the yard. The 1984 award rests on the museum's own page. The FFLA list (firelookout.org) labels the site Replica but cites the same NHLR entry (US 328, WA 34). The 2025 article says visits have tapered off; confirm the current booking route before publishing. The museum page is self-description by the operator. Access is set to restricted because visits are by appointment, not open at will.
